# Was the Dropbox outage on Nov 20 a cyberattack?

**Reported.** Reported, on Dropbox's own account: its status page says the outage was not caused by a cyberattack or by AI acting on its own. No independent source has confirmed that, and Dropbox has not given a cause.

Incident: Dropbox outage, Nov 20, 2026. Also reported as the Dropbox outage. First published Nov 21, 2026; last updated Nov 21, 2026, 1:23 AM ET.

> **Not verified: initial investigation only.** Nothing on this page is absolutely confirmed. It is an early look based only on publicly available sources, and it should not be treated as verified fact. Even items labeled "Confirmed" only mean a public source reports them. Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by Dropbox, any government agency, news outlet, company, or anyone else named.

This is the current answer, not a final verdict.

## The latest

Nov 21, 2026, 1:23 AM ET: **Dropbox says its 45-minute outage on Nov 20 was not a cyberattack. It has not said what caused it.** First draft. 5 sources (3 Tier 1, 2 Tier 3), 8 claims (4 Confirmed, 4 Not established), 5 questions. The outage and its times are confirmed by Dropbox's own status page. The denial of a cyberattack is Dropbox's own statement and no independent source backs it, so the main question is labelled Reported. No cause, user count or post-incident report found. No link to other outages is shown. Dropbox Sign was named in a request but is not on the status page, so it is not listed. Privacy check done: no names of private people, no handles, no contact details.

## At a glance

- Status: monitoring
- Size: Large. Dropbox is a service many people and businesses use daily, and its status page rated this outage Critical. It lasted about 45 minutes. Dropbox has not said how many people were affected.
- Who is affected: People and teams who use Dropbox's website, apps, API, Paper, Passwords, Dash, Protect, Replay, DocSend or MCP Server, or its support services, between 2:28 PM and 3:13 PM ET on Friday, Nov 20. Everything is shown as operational again.

### Known so far

- Dropbox's status page shows an incident from 2:28 PM to 3:13 PM ET on Nov 20, about 45 minutes.
- The status page rated it Critical, with the website, apps and API in major outage along with several other Dropbox services.
- Dropbox said the outage was not caused by a cyberattack or by AI acting on its own. This is the company's own statement, not an independent finding.

### Not known yet

- What caused the outage. Dropbox has not said.
- Whether it was a cyberattack. Dropbox says it was not; no independent source has confirmed that.
- How many users were affected.
- Whether it has any link to other outages this month. No source shows one.
